note: Village of Lynch RV park on the south side of town (4th St & Railroad Ave), a short walk from the main street; Ponca Creek is beyond the trees to the south-east. Back-in gravel pads in grass with tables and fire pits, a covered picnic area. Pay at a bar downtown or call for pickup; no reservations. Grass can be long and neighbouring dogs noisy (2024 review). CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $25 a night in July 2024 (The Dyrt and Campendium reviews); the village has no web page (2026-11-05). --Claude
summary: No village web page; priced from two dated July 2024 camper reports at $25 (fees added, reported). Count 9 from a 2024 review + imagery; 50 A + water + sewer at every site; showers. Pin on the pads. Not waterfront confirmed. Phone 402-569-3003 unverified (VisitNebraska-only, blocked).
flags: PRESENCE / WEB: the Village of Lynch has no website I could find; the stored website is the VisitNebraska tourism listing (Cloudflare-blocked, unread). Google's panel (4.7 from 3 reviews) has no phone or website. Directories (The Dyrt, Campendium) are the only readable sources. As a municipal park it is not under the private gate, but nothing official confirms it is still run; the newest dated report is July 2024.
PHONE 402-569-3003 unverified: it rests on the VisitNebraska listing; the 2024 Dyrt review mentions 'you can call a number' without giving it. Keep it but treat as weak.
OWNERSHIP: The Dyrt's summary says 'operates under county management'; the stored note and VisitNebraska say village/city. No operator page settles it; local either way.
PIN OK: stored 42.82817,-98.46687 sits on the north end of the pad row; Google 42.82791,-98.46675 is 30 m south.
WATERFRONT not waterfront confirmed: Ponca Creek is ~150 m south-east behind a tree belt and houses.

SEASON: stored year_round false (Allstays 'March through November' per web search snippet); not verified from any operator source, left as stored. max_rig_ft 45 from the Dyrt summary ('RVs up to 45 feet') - left as stored.
Sites are back-ins on gravel with grass between; a 2024 Campendium report counted 6, the Dyrt review 9-10; imagery shows about nine pads.
